newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit firms after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit firms after volatile session.

text.p: The ringgit firmed against the dollar after a volatile session, helped by a sharply higher-than-expected March trade surplus, dealers said.
Malaysia posted a a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March against a surplus of 368.5 million in February.
"It was a roller-coaster ride for dollar/ringgit, but the ringgit stayed firm after the trade figures," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
The ringgit jumped sharply to a high of 2.4735 a dollar in early trade from an opening around 2.4900 on massive selling of dollar/ringgit positions by offshore players.
It was quoted at 2.4870/90 a dollar at 1000 GMT against 2.5065 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
Talk that Bank Negara had cut off offshore players' access to the local swap market prompted funds to unwind their long dollar positions.
The central bank denied it had issued instructions to banks to stop undertaking swap transactions.
But local banks have been reluctant to quote to offshore players, causing funds to sell dollars on the spot market and to cover their short ringgit positions, dealers said.
Bank Negara said in a statement the shortage of ringgit in the market was a temporary phenomenon resulting from speculative activities.
Dealers said foreign funds were still trying to get out of their positions and the dollar would be sold on any rallies against the ringgit.
"For the moment, I think dollar/ringgit will be kept between 2.4750 and 2.4950," said a dealer with a European bank in Kuala Lumpur.

The ringgit's strength was also supported by firmer interest rates due to the liquidity squeeze. The tightening started after Bank Negara's aggressive intervention in the foreign exchange market on Wednesday to stem a slide in the ringgit.
The overnight interbank rate traded as high as 20 percent from 8.5 percent on Thursday.
